Q: Tkinter does not display Frames correctly after grid_remove() under macOS A:

Thank you all for your suggestions. In the end, I opted for the solution proposed by @TheLizzard. I want to share what I did so people encountering this bug have a (hacky) solution at least. If it is against guidelines to post this as an answer, please let me know. So what I found out is the following: giving Frames an event bind for <Enter> or <Leave> does not help on its own. The binding has to trigger a configure on an element (only tested it with .configure(bg="color") so maybe other uses of configure do not work).

I created a widget like this:

import tkinter as tk

class Updater(tk.Frame):
    def __init__(self, parent, height, width)
        # ececec is the default frame color under OSX 10.13.6
        tk.Frame.__init__(self, parent, height=height, width=width, bg="#ececec")
        self.grid_propagate(False)
        self.bind("<Enter>", self.triggerDisplay)
        self.bind("<Leave>", self.triggerDisplay)

    def triggerDisplay(self, event):
        self.configure(bg="#ececec")

Then I put a 1x1 wide version of this widget onto every one of my pages in the topmost left corner. The effect is that the page will display instantly if the mouse pointer enters or leaves the topmost left corner (0,0). I then simply added a method to the class that handles page transitions, which moves the mouse pointer to (0,0), being the topmost left corner of the page, like this:

def moveToCorner(self):
    self.update_idletasks()
    self.event_generate("<Motion>", warp=True, x=0, y=0)

Lastly, I call moveToCorner() on every page transition, and my application displays pages like it should.

If the code contains typos, it's because I typed it by hand (because I could not copy it out of my VM).

Q: AuthJS Session Customization A:

This is expected behavior in Auth.js v5.

In the authorized() callback you are running in middleware, and middleware does not get custom fields on auth.user. Only the default fields (name, email, image) exist there. Your role and user_id are correctly stored — they live on the JWT token, not on auth.user.

So this line will always be undefined:

const role = auth?.user?.role;

Read it from the token instead:

const role = auth?.token?.role;

Your jwt and session callbacks are already correct.

The bug is just reading the role from the wrong place.

Q: How to fix "The target principal name is incorrect error" with Microsoft.Data.SqlClient Version=4.0.0 A:

Do not do this in production. This answer is for troubleshooting purposes only.

AlwaysLearning posted the answer in the comments:

The target principal name is incorrect signifies that the Name or IP Address you're using in the Server=...; portion of your connection string does not match a CommonName or SubjectAltName in the X.509 certificate provided by the SQL Server which isn't surprising because, by default, SQL Server installs with a self-signed certificate using only the current host name. Does the error go away if you include TrustServerCertificate=False; in (all of) your connection strings?

Argh, replace TrustServerCertificate=False; with TrustServerCertificate=True; ... it's meant to trust whatever certificate is presented regardless of the CommonName, SubjectAltName(s) and certificate chain.

So the answer was

TrustServerCertificate=True

*Adding this to accurately show that the question has been answered. Community Wikis do not generate points, so this is not an attempt to steal points. AlwaysLearning should post the answer to get credit.

Q: Ajax not populating dropdown if selected too fast A:

add this just as you enter the change event of your #select_show select

$('#province').attr('disabled', true);

this will disable the select, meaning the user won't be able to click on it manually (this is open to javascript hacks, tho). Then when you're sure all your locations have been fetched, just turn it back to false

$('#province').attr('disabled', false);

which will of course re-enable the input to let the user use it.

note that there's probably alot of other ways to work around that problem, but that way was just the first that came up to my mind!

Q: Enabling sudo mode during project configuration in VS Code A:

When I configure a project using VS Code, I get, , for example, an error:

[cmake] CMake Error at /Proj/contrib/boost/contrib/build/cmake/lib/CMakeLists.txt:122 (configure_file):
[cmake]   Operation not permitted

When calling the CMake method

configure_file("${LIBRARY_DIR}/file1" "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/file2" @ONLY)

Even chmod -R 777 Proj doesn't help.
If I run the command that VS Code generates from the terminal, I get the same error. But if I run the same command with sudo, everything is fine.

To avoid such problems, I would like to know how to prefix the command generated by the VS Code.

Q: How to get the data from a Laravel relationship without loading it onto the initial model A:

Today I faced a common Laravel issue and wanted to share the solution for anyone who runs into the same problem.

I didn’t want to add the relationship to the parent model or remove or unset the relation afterwards or modify the model’s JSON / array output.

I only wanted the result of the relationship query, fetched separately.

You cannot retrieve a relationship via the property without mutating the parent model.
This is expected Laravel behavior.

In Laravel, there are two different ways to access relationships:

Accessing as a property (mutates the model)

$posts = $user->posts;

  • This lazy-loads the relationship

  • Laravel stores it internally

  • $user is now considered to have a posts attribute

  • It will appear in toArray() / JSON output

  • This behavior is intentional and unavoidable

Accessing as a method (does NOT mutate the model)

posts = $user->posts()->get();

  • Executes a query

  • Returns the related models

  • Does NOT attach anything to $user

  • $user remains unchanged
